topic: Port and Harbour Safety: Risks and Controls Explained · How misdeclared weight creates downstream risk (3/4)

passage.text: Containers sometimes have a wrong weight written on their documents. This is a serious and repeated cause of accidents. The person who writes the wrong weight is almost never the person who gets hurt. Instead, the risk tends to move to the crane operator and the workers who secure the cargo with ropes and chains. These workers face the danger, not the person who made the mistake. Well-managed terminals check the container weight at the gate. They do not simply trust the documents. If the declared weight does not match the real weight, they stop the operation. They do not treat it as just a small paperwork error.
